mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, and this relationship is always active without requiring a threshold condition.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day forward returns is positive (i.e., lower FEDFUNDS is associated with negative returns) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 300, it signals persistent inflation that triggers monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 300 and 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is above 300, it indicates a policy response to inflation that compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 2.0 and CPIAUCSL > 300, the 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDPC1 growth > 2% and HOUST > 1500), S&P 500 forward returns are negative over the next 20 trading days due to overvaluation and policy tightening expectations.
failure_condition: In periods where GDPC1 growth > 2% and HOUST > 1500, the 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, and this relationship is always active without requiring a threshold condition.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO and 60-day forward returns is positive (i.e., higher INDPRO is associated with negative returns) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.0%, it signals a tight labor market that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 3.0 and 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) is above 100k and unemployment (UNRATE) is below 3.5%, it indicates a strong labor market that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 100000 and UNRATE < 3.5, the 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) exceed 680000, it signals strong consumer demand that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 680000 and 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
